name: Easal

attributes.attribute: king of the Golden Pillars who aided the Sons of Tuireann
three warriors bound to a dozen near-impossible feats
magical animals that died daily yet returned in fine health
the great god of abundance who owned self-restoring pigs

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Easal was a king of the Golden Pillars in Irish legend. He appears in a tale called the Sons of Tuireann. That tale is one of the Three Sorrows of Ireland. Three young warriors were bound to a dozen near-impossible feats. They did this to pay for killing their father's enemies. They would have died without Easal's help. He fed them from magical pigs. These pigs were killed each day and eaten each evening. Yet each morning they foraged in fine health. Their flesh also protected a person from any disease. Easal may reflect the Dagda, the great god of abundance. The Dagda also owned self-restoring pigs.

okr.objective: Present Easal as the king whose magical pigs saved the Sons of Tuireann.
key_results: Easal appears in the tale of the Sons of Tuireann, a Three Sorrow of Ireland.
